feature: Agentic AI Framework for Life Sciences
description: Purpose-built agentic AI capabilities that bring intelligent, operational assistance directly into life sciences workflows. The framework analyzes complex clinical and patient data, aligns to regulated processes, and empowers teams from the clinic to the field to take real action. Each agent is composed of three parts: Skills (prebuilt flows for domain jobs), Topics (focus the agent on a defined task type), and Actions (executable steps like generating summaries, retrieving records, or updating data).
setup_steps: Enable the agentic AI framework in your org
Assign the appropriate life sciences AI permission sets to users
Configure topics relevant to your use cases (clinical, patient, commercial)
Map standard and custom actions to each topic
Configure grounding data sources per topic using the data unification layer
Define human oversight rules for sensitive or irreversible actions
Test agent responses in sandbox before production deployment
prerequisites: Industry cloud licenses assigned to users
Data unification layer (Data 360) configured for cross-system data access
Permission sets for AI features assigned
Relevant data model objects populated (accounts, contacts, visits, products)
Trust layer configuration for data protection boundaries
configuration_details: Agents are configured with clicks by admins and extended by developers on the platform
Each agent has scoped Topics that constrain what it can discuss
Actions map to Flows, Apex classes, or API calls the agent can invoke
Grounding sources should be scoped per topic — a patient-support topic should not access commercial prescribing data
Agent actions run in user context — subject to the same field-level security and sharing rules as manual user actions
Separate suggest-only from act actions — read-only vs. write/external actions require different oversight levels
All agent actions are logged at the same fidelity as human user actions for audit trails
objects_and_fields: Permission Set assignments for AI features
integration_patterns: Agent actions invoke the same governed automation (Flow, Apex, integration) that a human user would trigger
Grounding uses Data 360 federation — no need to copy all data into the platform
Agents sit above the application layer, not beside it — inheriting sharing rules and security
External data retrieved as context is treated as untrusted data, not as instructions (prompt injection defense)
gotchas: CRITICAL: Never give an agent broader access than the human user it acts on behalf of
Agent summarizations can create data leaks by aggregating across security boundaries a human user could not cross
Ground narrowly per topic — grounding against all data sources means every topic can surface every dataset
Prompt injection is a live threat — content from external sources (emails, documents) can contain instructions aimed at the model
Agents should not auto-communicate to patients or healthcare providers without human review
For clinical claims, never use open web grounding — only approved medical content
Do not reach for an agent just because it is available — use deterministic automation (Flows) when the task has one correct answer and full input data
migration_relevance: Veeva CRM has no native agentic AI layer — migration to the target platform adds AI-powered visit preparation, call summaries, benefits verification, and site selection that are absent in Veeva. The modular skill/topic/action architecture allows incremental adoption. Migration teams should map existing Veeva processes to determine which are candidates for AI augmentation vs. deterministic automation.

description: AI-assisted site feasibility and selection for clinical trials. Helps site feasibility leads identify top sites and investigators for a research study by analyzing historical enrollment data, site capability, investigator history, and therapeutic expertise.
setup_steps: Configure the Clinical Trial Management skill in the agentic AI framework
Set up the Site Selection Assistance topic
Enable the standard actions: Get site search filters, Add site search results, Summarize site and investigator, Send feasibility assessments
Populate site and investigator data in the platform
Configure grounding against historical enrollment and site capability data
Define human oversight rules — study team makes the final selection, agent narrows the list
prerequisites: Clinical trial data model objects populated (ResearchStudy, ResearchStudySite, etc.)
Historical enrollment data available for grounding
Site and investigator profiles maintained
Clinical AI permission sets assigned
configuration_details: Topic: Site Selection Assistance — assists site feasibility leads in identifying top sites and investigators

Actions include: Get site search filters for research study, Add site search results/site/investigators to research study, Summarize site and investigator, Send site feasibility assessments to site contacts
Agent narrows the list — human team makes the final selection
Grounding uses historical enrollment data, site capability data, and investigator history
integration_patterns: Can integrate with external CTMS/EDC systems via scheduled batch or event-driven status updates
The platform orchestrates and tracks status — the EDC/CTMS remains system of record for clinical data
Platform Events for milestone-driven clinical trial status changes
gotchas: The platform is not the system of record for detailed clinical data — that belongs to the EDC/CTMS
Agent recommendations are suggestions — study team must review and approve site selections
Grounding must be scoped to clinical data only — commercial data should not bleed into clinical topics
Historical enrollment data quality directly impacts recommendation quality
migration_relevance: Veeva CRM does not natively support clinical trial site selection. This is a net-new capability that significantly accelerates trial startup. For organizations migrating from Veeva who also have clinical operations, this reduces dependency on separate CTMS tools for site feasibility assessment.

description: AI-assisted benefits reverification for patient services representatives. Helps reps reverify pharmacy benefits for program enrollees, draft or revise benefits verification emails, and summarize patient responses — accelerating time-consuming insurance verification processes.
setup_steps: Configure the Patient Services skill in the agentic AI framework
Set up the Benefits Reverification topic
Enable standard actions: Draft or revise benefits verification email, Summarize patient response
Configure integration with payer/benefits data sources
Set up Pharmacy Benefits Verification tab on Care Program Enrollee records
Define human oversight rules — results shown to human agent, not auto-communicated to patient
prerequisites: Patient services data model configured (CareProgramEnrollee, VerificationRequest, BenefitInformation)
Integration with payer/benefits systems for real-time or cached lookups
Patient services permission sets assigned
Service Cloud components configured for case management and omni-channel routing
configuration_details: Topic: Benefits Reverification — assists patient services reps in reverifying benefits for program enrollees
Actions: Draft or revise benefits verification email, Summarize patient response
Pharmacy Benefits Verification tab displays verification requests and benefit information for a patient
Benefits data retrieved via governed integration — not stored permanently
Real-time formulary or benefits checks use synchronous external service calls, cached briefly
Results shown to human agent first — never auto-communicated to patients
integration_patterns: Synchronous external service call for real-time formulary/benefits check, with brief caching
Governed integration for payer data — not stored permanently in the platform
Service Cloud underneath for case management and omni-channel routing
AI-generated case summaries from Service agents log outcomes and key details of patient support calls
gotchas: Benefits data should not be stored permanently — use caching with TTL
Full replication of payer data would always be stale — use real-time lookups
Patient support topic should not have healthcare provider prescribing data in its retrieval scope
Human agent handoff required for anything ambiguous or emotionally sensitive
Patient-identifiable data fields should use encryption (Shield Platform Encryption)
migration_relevance: Veeva CRM has limited patient services capabilities and no AI-assisted benefits verification. This is a significant upgrade for organizations that currently manage benefits verification manually or through disconnected systems. The automation can dramatically reduce time-to-therapy for patients.

description: AI-powered visit preparation for key account managers, medical science liaisons (MSLs), and field representatives. Generates contextual summaries of healthcare providers including engagement history, consent status, recent content interactions, prescribing trends, and open items to help reps prepare for every interaction.
setup_steps: Configure the Customer Engagement skill in the agentic AI framework
Set up the Visit Planning topic
Enable standard actions: Generate healthcare provider summary, Identify records by name
Configure grounding against engagement history, territory data, product data, and prior visit notes
Set up mobile access for field users
Define human oversight rules — agent suggests, rep reviews before the call
prerequisites: Commercial data model populated (Accounts, Visits, Products, Territory assignments)
Engagement history data available
Consent management configured for healthcare providers
Territory alignment configured
Mobile offline capabilities enabled
configuration_details: Topic: Visit Planning — helps reps prepare for visits with contextual summaries
Actions: Generate healthcare provider summary, Identify records by name
Pre-call summaries include: key affiliations, licensure, consent status, segmentation, engagement history, recent content interactions
Agent suggests talking points and open items — rep reviews before the call, agent does not message the provider directly
Can combine with Sales agent capabilities for drafting personalized, compliant follow-up messages after a visit
Smart Summary appears on Dashboard tab of healthcare provider accounts
integration_patterns: Grounding uses engagement history, consent status, recent content sent from platform data
Can federate external prescribing/market data via Data 360 without copying into the platform
Mobile-first design — field reps access on devices
Offline data cached locally with encryption at rest; syncs when connectivity returns
gotchas: Agent should not have write authority for summarization actions — read-only output for account summarization
Territory alignment is a business attribute, not a security mechanism — do not assume alignment implements sharing
Summarization must not aggregate across security boundaries (clinical + commercial data)
Offline validation rules are deferred, not skipped — design validation to tolerate offline ordering
Automation triggered by offline visits fires when device reconnects, not in real-time
migration_relevance: Veeva CRM provides call/visit tracking but has no native AI-powered visit preparation or HCP summarization. Migration to the target platform adds intelligent pre-call briefings that synthesize engagement history, consent status, and content interactions — capabilities that required manual effort or third-party tools in Veeva. The modular topic/action architecture means this can be enabled incrementally post-migration.

description: AI-assisted handling of medical information requests from healthcare providers. Accurately answers clinical questions using only approved medical content, with escalation to medical information specialists for anything outside approved content boundaries.
setup_steps: Configure the Medical Information topic in the agentic AI framework
Load approved medical content into the grounding data source
CRITICAL: Disable open web grounding for clinical claims — only approved content
Configure escalation rules for medical information specialists
Set up audit logging for all medical information interactions
prerequisites: Approved medical content library maintained and loaded
Medical information specialist escalation path configured
Medical affairs permission sets assigned
Compliance and audit framework configured
configuration_details: Grounding MUST use only approved medical content — never open web for clinical claims
Escalation to medical information specialist for anything outside approved content
All interactions logged with full audit trail (what action ran, what data it touched, what output it returned)
Agent should not provide diagnoses or unsupported clinical guidance
integration_patterns: Content management system integration for approved medical content (metadata in platform, content in CMS)
Escalation workflow to medical affairs team
Full audit logging for regulatory compliance
gotchas: CRITICAL: Never use open web grounding for clinical claims — only approved medical content
All medical information responses require audit trail
Agent must not make unsupported clinical claims
Escalation path must be clearly defined and tested
Content from external sources treated as untrusted data for prompt injection defense
migration_relevance: Veeva CRM handles medical inquiries through Veeva Medical but without AI-powered response generation. The target platform adds AI-assisted response drafting grounded in approved content, reducing response time while maintaining compliance. This is particularly valuable for medical affairs teams handling high volumes of healthcare provider inquiries.

description: AI agent that assists field representatives with tasks like logging visits from voice notes, drafting follow-up communications, and updating records. The rep reviews and approves all generated content before it saves.
setup_steps: Enable field rep assistance topic in the agentic AI framework
Configure voice-to-text capabilities for visit logging
Set up mobile agent access for field users
Configure human oversight rules — rep reviews and approves generated records before saving
Enable offline mode for field usage
prerequisites: Mobile app configured for field users
Visit/Interaction data model set up
Offline sync framework configured
Field rep permission sets assigned
configuration_details: Agent converts voice notes into structured visit records
Rep MUST review and approve the generated record before it saves — no auto-save
Works on mobile devices in field conditions
Integrates with visit/interaction tracking
During visits, reps can log insights, launch samples, or share approved content from mobile
Afterward, reps document the visit, update product ratings, and schedule follow-ups in one flow
integration_patterns: Mobile-first with offline capability
Voice-to-text processing
Sync engine handles offline-created records
Platform Events for follow-up automation fire on reconnect
gotchas: Offline-created records sync with delay — automation fires on reconnect, not in real-time
Validation rules are deferred during offline use, not skipped
Conflict handling needs explicit policy — last-write-wins may not be appropriate for compliance-sensitive fields
Local device storage must be encrypted; remote wipe policy required for lost/stolen devices
Sync should limit data footprint — do not sync entire territory history to every device
migration_relevance: Veeva CRM mobile (iPad-focused) supports visit logging but has no AI-powered voice-to-visit or automated record generation. Migration adds voice-based visit capture, AI-drafted follow-ups, and intelligent next-best-action recommendations that are absent in the Veeva mobile experience.

description: Security and governance framework that mediates what the underlying AI model sees and returns. Ensures data protection, auditability, and policy-aware automation for all agentic AI interactions in regulated life sciences environments.
setup_steps: Configure Trust Layer policies for data protection boundaries
Set up role-based access controls for AI features
Configure audit logging for all agent interactions
Define consent management rules for AI-driven outreach
Set up data masking for non-production environments
prerequisites: Security model designed (object/field-level security, record-level access, sharing rules)
Permission Set Groups configured for role-based access
Shield Platform Encryption enabled for sensitive fields
Event Monitoring configured for access auditing
configuration_details: Data stays within the platform trust boundary
Access controlled using role-based permissions and consent
Agents keep records of what they did, why, and which sources they used
Actions follow defined rules including disclosure tracking, electronic signatures, and retention policies
Agent actions must run in user context — same field-level security and sharing rules as manual actions
Separate suggest from act — irreversible actions require human confirmation
Log everything an agent does at the same fidelity as human user actions
objects_and_fields: Permission Set Groups (e.g., Field Rep - Oncology, Medical Science Liaison, Patient Services Agent)
integration_patterns: Integration users must follow least-privilege principle — only specific fields, not system admin
Data masking required in non-production environments
Event Monitoring detects bulk export of sensitive data outside normal patterns
gotchas: A service account with elevated privileges powering the agent defeats the entire access model
Grounding against all data because it is convenient means every topic can surface every dataset
Agent summarization that aggregates across a security boundary is a security failure even if no single query was unauthorized
Content ingested from external sources can contain prompt injection instructions
Do not treat all life sciences implementations as having the same regulatory requirements — GxP, GDPR, HIPAA, 21 CFR Part 11 applicability varies by organization, country, process, and data
migration_relevance: Veeva CRM has its own compliance framework but lacks an integrated AI trust layer. Migration to the target platform requires careful mapping of existing security models and compliance requirements. The built-in Trust Layer provides native support for GxP, GDPR, HIPAA, and 21 CFR Part 11 requirements that would need separate tooling in a Veeva environment.

feature: Advanced Therapy Management with AI Orchestration
description: AI-supported management of advanced therapies such as cell and gene treatments. Supports multistep scheduling, digital chain of custody, electronic signatures, and care orchestration across stakeholders. Platform AI can assist with care coordination and status tracking.
setup_steps: Configure Care Program and Care Program Enrollee objects
Set up multistep scheduling workflows
Enable digital chain of custody tracking
Configure electronic signature capabilities
Set up care orchestration automation
Optionally enable AI-assisted care coordination summaries
prerequisites: Care Program data model configured
Participant enrollment workflows set up
Electronic signature infrastructure configured
Chain of custody tracking objects enabled
Patient consent management configured
configuration_details: Care Program Enrollee records track patient progress through therapy stages (e.g., Apheresis stage for gene therapy)
Multistep scheduling coordinates across multiple stakeholders
Digital chain of custody provides full tracking of therapy materials
E-signatures satisfy audit and retention requirements
AI can generate coordination summaries and surface next steps
Secure portals allow patients to self-register and access pre-screening instructions
integration_patterns: Integration with laboratory systems for chain of custody
EHR/EMR integration for patient clinical data (synchronous REST, narrowly scoped)
Platform Events for milestone notifications
Regulatory/adverse-event reporting via synchronous API with confirmed receipt and audit log
gotchas: PHI-heavy data — retrieve only what is needed at the point of use
EHR integration should be synchronous REST, narrowly scoped — not bulk replication
Regulatory adverse-event reporting requires confirmed, timestamped submission — fire-and-forget events are not sufficient
Patient and healthcare provider data have different consent regimes and retention rules — keep graphs separate
E-signature and retention policies must satisfy specific regulatory audits
migration_relevance: Veeva CRM does not natively support advanced therapy management workflows. This is a net-new capability area for organizations migrating from Veeva. The platform provides purpose-built objects and workflows for cell and gene therapy coordination that would require extensive custom development on Veeva.

description: AI-enhanced actionable plans that generate standardized outreach and follow-up strategies. Clinical teams can use core capabilities to generate outreach plans for investigators identified during site selection, combining industry-specific AI skills with platform automation.
setup_steps: Configure Actionable Plans feature
Set up plan templates for different use cases (clinical outreach, commercial follow-up)
Enable AI integration for plan generation
Configure automation triggers for plan execution
Set up monitoring and completion tracking
prerequisites: Actionable Plans feature enabled
Relevant data model objects populated
AI framework configured with appropriate topics
User permission sets assigned
configuration_details: Plans combine industry-specific AI skills with platform automation
Templates define standard outreach sequences and follow-up cadences
AI can suggest plan modifications based on historical engagement data
Plans execute through governed automation paths (Flow, Apex)
Completion tracking provides visibility into plan execution status
integration_patterns: Plans invoke the same governed automation as manual user actions
Can combine with email automation from Sales agent capabilities
Data 360 grounding for AI-suggested plan modifications
gotchas: Plans should follow the same sharing and security rules as manual actions
AI-suggested modifications should be reviewed before execution
Do not conflate plan execution authority with plan viewing authority
migration_relevance: Veeva CRM has Suggestions and MyInsights but lacks platform-native actionable plans with AI integration. Migration enables standardized, AI-enhanced outreach workflows that combine the best of deterministic automation with intelligent recommendations.

description: The central data unification engine that powers agentic AI. Securely connects and harmonizes data from all sources including patient records, clinical trial data in data lakes, and information from external electronic health records (EHR) or lab systems. Provides the foundation for accurate AI by ensuring every agent action is informed by a complete and trusted data picture.
setup_steps: Configure Data 360 data streams from relevant sources
Set up identity resolution rules for healthcare providers and organizations
Define golden record ownership and conflict handling
Configure federation for data that does not need to be copied into the platform
Set up data refresh schedules per source
Scope grounding sources per AI topic
prerequisites: Data 360 licenses assigned
Source system connectivity configured (EHR, CTMS, MDM, data lakes)
Identity resolution matching rules defined
Data governance framework established
configuration_details: Identity resolution handles noisy inputs — different spellings, manual entries, and NPI-linked records
Define matching rules, golden-record ownership, conflict handling, update frequency per source
Country-specific identifiers may require different matching strategies per region
Zero-copy federation for data you need to reason over but do not want to duplicate
Route high-volume analytical data into Data 360 rather than custom objects
Grounding sources should be scoped per AI topic — not blanket access to all data
objects_and_fields: Data Model Objects (DMOs) for harmonized data
integration_patterns: Zero-copy federation for external datasets — no replication needed for AI grounding
Batch/CDC via integration middleware for synchronized master data
Bulk API for large scheduled data loads into Data 360
Real-time lookups via synchronous external service calls with brief caching
gotchas: Data 360 is not a replacement for the object model — it is a companion to it
A matching strategy that works in one country may not work in another
Every replicated field is a future sync-conflict and drift risk — prefer federation
Do not assume 'we might need it later' is sufficient justification to store data permanently
Grounding an agent against all of Data 360 means every topic can surface every dataset — scope narrowly
migration_relevance: Veeva CRM relies on Veeva Network (now Veeva Compass) for master data management but has no equivalent of Data 360 for unified AI grounding. Migration should map existing Veeva Network data flows to Data 360 identity resolution and determine which external data sources to federate vs. replicate. This is the foundational layer that enables all AI capabilities on the target platform.
